entries.evidence: MANUAL-REVIEW CANDIDATE per gate instructions. Official PDF (docs/client-source/CATALOGO DE DECANTS.pdf, page 34) labels this only 'BIR Intense' -- an abbreviation, decoded from an overlapping text layer (see supabase/staging/pdf-2026-commercial-reconciliation.json:bir_intense and row_reconciliation, match_basis=DECODED_OVERLAPPING_PDF_TEXT_LAYER) -- it does NOT itself spell out 'Burberry Brit Intense'. Client photo img/perfumes/Burberry Burberry Brit Intense.png shows a charcoal/gunmetal rectangular bottle with a tonal check (nova-check) texture and silver cap, which visually matches Burberry's 2011 'Brit Intense' bottle design. Burberry has since discontinued this line; no current official Burberry product page exists to size-check against. Secondary references (Fragrantica/retail) for the closest matching discontinued Burberry 'Intense' men's flanker ('Brit Rhythm for Him Intense', 2013) show 90 ml EDT, not 100 ml EDP -- but that is a visually different (2013) bottle design, so it is not certain to be the same product as the client's photographed bottle.
entries.notes: IDENTITY_CONFIRMED at the brand+line level (Burberry Brit Intense) via client photography, which is stronger evidence here than the abbreviated/decoded PDF label. However concentration (repo EDP vs. likely EDT) and exact ml are NOT independently confirmable against a live official source because the product is discontinued. Recorded as SIZE_CONFLICT / concentration-unverified rather than guessed. Do not silently correct; this is the exact case Section D says to leave unresolved and report. Also relevant: assets/data.js:472 previously set legacy_hidden=true (2026-09-06 CLIENT_CONFIRMED, no stock), superseded for decant pricing purposes only by the 2026-09-13 PDF instruction per pdf-2026-commercial-reconciliation.json -- that supersession note does not extend to size/concentration.

Official rabanne.com product page and major retailers (Sephora, Jomashop, FragranceX) sell this exclusively as 'Invictus Victory Elixir' -- there is no standalone 'Victory Elixir' product independent of the Invictus line. Brand (Paco Rabanne / Rabanne) and bottle art are correct, and the 100 ml size is correct, so this is a naming-completeness/concentration conflict, not a wrong-fragrance conflict. IMPORTANT CROSS-REFERENCE: supabase/staging/legacy-catalog-staging.json also contains a SEPARATE legacy_id 'invictus-elixir' ('Invictus Elixir', decants only, identical 3/5/10 ml prices 24/32/51, no bottle variant) that scripts/commercial-reconciliation.mjs already archives via PRODUCT_LIFECYCLE_OVERRIDES as 'V2-only; absent from the current authoritative client PDF'. This corroborates that 'victory-elixir' (with the bottle variant audited here) is the live/current record for this fragrance and 'invictus-elixir' is a superseded duplicate -- do not merge or rename 'victory-elixir' into/onto 'invictus-elixir' or vice versa; they must stay two distinct historical rows. Left unresolved -- Section D says do not rename merely for modern branding unless identity correctness requires it; adding the 'Invictus' qualifier is arguably required for identity correctness (it is not merely rebranding) but is left for an explicit follow-up decision rather than corrected silently in this gate, especially given this pre-existing duplicate-identity history.

readiness_contract.statement: PRODUCT CURRENTNESS/VISIBILITY, VARIANT COMMERCIAL READINESS, and PRICE AUTHORITY are three separate concepts. Variant-level publish_eligibility/blockers on each supabase/staging/commercial-reconciliation.json products[].variants[] entry are authoritative for that variant's own commercial readiness. Product-level products[].blockers is an audit rollup of child-variant issues -- it is NOT a storefront visibility gate and must never be read as 'all variants of this product are unpublishable'. A product with clean official_pdf decant variants (3/5/10 ml) and one legacy/provisional bottle variant must keep its decants individually publishable; the bottle's own blocker(s) stay scoped to the bottle variant only.
readiness_contract.future_obligation: 4K2 storefront/read-model code MUST evaluate variant-level readiness (publish_eligibility + blockers on the variant) when deciding whether to show/sell a specific variant. It MUST NOT use the product-level blockers array to hide sibling variants that are individually clean.
readiness_contract.scope_of_this_gate: No schema/field change and no new machine field were added -- the existing product vs. variant blockers/publish_eligibility fields in commercial-reconciliation.json already express this distinction unambiguously (see 4K-B2B.1 tests). Only the semantic contract and its consumption rule are documented and locked here, per Section F ('smallest implementation').
